record.name: pi-stack
record.description: Windows pi rig layout, pi 0.85.1 on glm-5.3-flash, MCP parity, the isession keep-alive hang
record.body:
Rebuilt 2026-07-28 by running erenwork's DRILL-ERENHOME. The pre-drill stack (loose `~/.pi/agent`, adapter at `~/dev/pi-mcp-adapter`, `memoirs-subconscious-pi`) is GONE — backup at `~/.pi/agent.old`. See [clan-members](../../shared/harness-infra/clan-members.md), [memoirs-ingest](/unfiled/memoirs-ingest.md).

## Layout

- `~/.pi/agent` is now a **git clone of `esinecan/erenworkpi`** (drill ran at `135c933`). It is a real repo — `git pull` updates the rig, and local edits show as a dirty tree.
- All rig dependencies live under `~/rig/` (12 repos): `pi-mcp-adapter` (branch `local-timeout-patch-on-pr72`, NOT main), `cortex-generic` (= `esinecan/cortex`, not `forto-cortex`), `forum`, `deepthink`, `web-surfer-llm-cli`, `isession`, `gamebook`, `pi-queue`, `crucible`, and `extensions/{pi-memory, fff-subconscious-pi, voice-of-reason-pi}`.
- pi: `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.85.1` (npm global, updated 2026-09-06 from 0.84.2; 0.84.2 came 2026-08-16 from 0.84.1, which came 2026-08-09 from 0.83.0). `settings.json`: `defaultProvider=zai`, `defaultModel=glm-5.3-flash` (set 2026-09-06 at Eren's direction; it was glm-5.3 from 2026-08-16, and glm-5.2 before that). glm-5.3-flash costs $0.075/$0.25 per Mtok against glm-5.3's $1.4/$4.4, keeps the 1M context and the 131k output cap, and adds **image input** that glm-5.3 does not have. It is the weaker model, so a pi-collab consult that needs reasoning depth should pass `--provider zai --model glm-5.3` explicitly, `defaultThinkingLevel=max`, `packages` uses **absolute** `C:/Users/yepis/rig/...` paths.
- **Updating everything is `pi update --all`.** Bare `pi update` = `--self` only and prints "Extensions are skipped"; `--extensions` = packages only; `--models` (catalog refresh) is in *neither* and always needs its own run. Also `--extension <source>` for one package, `--force` to reinstall an already-latest pi.
- **The old EBUSY self-update block is no longer reproducing.** On 2026-08-01 `pi update` (self) failed on Windows because npm renames the package dir aside and that dir held a live directory handle; the workaround was staging into a scratch dir and `robocopy /MIR`-ing the **contents** over the global package. On 2026-08-09 a plain `pi update` went 0.83.0 → 0.84.1 cleanly with no process cleanup. Keep the robocopy trick in mind if EBUSY returns, but do not reach for it first.
- **pi 0.84.1 hard-requires a Node with zstd.** It ships undici 8.9.0, which advertises `zstd` in Accept-Encoding and then calls `zlib.createZstdDecompress` **with no feature detection** (`lib/web/fetch/index.js`, the `coding === 'zstd'` branch). On a Node without it the process dies mid-response: `uncaughtException: TypeError: zlib.createZstdDecompress is not a function`. Node got zstd in **v23.8.0**, backported into 22.x LTS. Verified on this box: `C:\Program Files\nodejs` **v24.11.1** → `function` (pi works); **fnm's default v22.13.1** → `undefined` (pi crashes). Two nodes are installed and **fnm is the trap** — `fnm list` shows `v22.13.1 default` plus a `system` alias, and in any shell where fnm's multishell shim wins PATH precedence pi runs on 22.13.1. **The symptom looks shell-dependent and is not** — PowerShell vs bash vs cmd is irrelevant, only which node is first on PATH. Diagnose with `Get-Command node -All` and `node -e "console.log(typeof require('zlib').createZstdDecompress)"`.
- `defaultThinkingLevel` accepts `minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`, but prefer `max`. glm-5.2's `thinkingLevelMap` only had keys for `minimal/low/medium/high/max` (**no `xhigh`**); glm-5.3 under `zai` ships no custom map, so the level passes through to `reasoning_effort` unchanged and `max` stays the safe choice.
- `auth.json` is `{}` — pi authenticates from User-scope env vars (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `ZAI_API_KEY`, `BRAVE_API_KEY`). MINIMAX deliberately not provisioned; nothing in the rig reads it.

## The render workflow — do not hand-edit mcp.json

`~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` and `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` are **generated**, not maintained. Run `~/.pi/agent/render-home.ps1` after any `git pull`. It renders `profiles/home/mcp.home.json` (substituting `__EHOME__`), then applies what the shared profile cannot express:

- rewrites `web-surfer` from erenwork's `sh -c 'set -a; . .env; exec node ...'` to `command: node` + `cwd` (no `sh` on a Windows PATH; `dist/mcp-server.js` calls `dotenv.config()` itself)
- **keeps `isession`** (since 2026-07-28; it used to drop it). Windows support is real now — see the ConPTY backend note below. It is a URL server. **FIXED 2026-08-01: `mcp.local.json` now overrides it to `lifecycle: lazy`** (the merge is `Add-Member -Force`, so local beats the template's `keep-alive`), which connects only on first use. Before that fix a dead endpoint was the single worst trap on this box: with `keep-alive`, the SSE transport enters a **30s reconnect loop that never gives up**, and a headless `pi -p` run then never produces an answer at all — not just a slow exit. It masquerades as an intermittent hang and will frame whatever server you added most recently. Diagnosis that actually worked: `Start-Process` with `-RedirectStandardOutput` and poll the file, because `| Out-String` buffers until exit and shows nothing. `startupTimeoutMs` does **not** bound it. Start the daemon with `python ~/rig/isession/isession/http_server.py --port 8765`; the render script still warns when nothing is listening.
- merges `profiles/home/mcp.local.json` — erenhome-only servers (`memoirs`, `apthunt`) that are not in erenworkpi and would otherwise vanish on every re-render.

`render-home.ps1` and `mcp.local.json` are in `.git/info/exclude`, so they never dirty the tracked repo or try to travel back to erenwork.

**Why a script and not `sed`:** the README's render step is `sed`, which does not exist here. And PowerShell 5.1's `Out-File -Encoding utf8` writes a **BOM**, which the adapter's `JSON.parse` rejects outright ("Unexpected token '﻿'"). Always write these files UTF-8 **without** BOM.

Live servers (14 since 2026-08-01): `serena` (uvx), `cortex-generic`, `forum`, `deepthink`, `web-surfer`, `memoirs`, `apthunt`, `isession`, plus the parity set added from Claude Code's `~/.claude.json` — `flaui`, `brave-search`, `google-workspace`, `linkedin`, `mcp-inspector`, `memory`.

All six parity servers live in `profiles/home/mcp.local.json` and are `lifecycle: lazy` — they connect on first use, so pi startup stays light. The adapter defaults to **proxy mode** (everything behind one `mcp` tool), so a server without `directTools` costs almost no context; adding servers is cheap. Only `flaui` (7 window tools) and `brave-search` (`brave_web_search`) were promoted to `directTools`. Not ported: `filesystem` (pi has native file tools + serena), `sequential-thinking` (deepthink covers it), `elevated-cmd` (pi has a native shell, and it isn't actually elevated — see [elevated-cmd-not-elevated](../tools-mcp/elevated-cmd-not-elevated.md)).

**Every key under `mcpServers` in `mcp.local.json` is merged as a server** — the render loop iterates property names blindly, so a `"_comment"` placed inside that object becomes a bogus server entry. Keep commentary at the file's top level.

## Local patches that are NOT upstream — re-apply if these repos are re-cloned

- `~/rig/extensions/voice-of-reason-pi/{index.js,gemini_worker.py,prompt.py}` — the critic now runs **Gemini `flash` via `gemini-mcp`**, headless, in a detached worker. Config is `config.json` (`model`, `headless`, `cooldown_seconds: 120`, `min_messages: 4`, `transcript_token_budget: 12000`, `max_critique_chars: 500`) plus `config.local.json` pinning the Gemini `account` to `yepis`. Env knobs are only `PI_VOICE_OF_REASON_{DEBUG,MAX_AGE_MS,WHEN}`. `prompt.py` merges two lineages: the tone and tool-awareness rules from the z.ai-era prompt, the `NO_COMMENT` sentinel and trust-boundary section from the Claude Code port. **History, in case a z.ai-shaped assumption resurfaces:** it was retargeted 2026-08-01 from deepseek-v4-pro to glm-5.2 on z.ai, then moved off z.ai onto Gemini on 2026-08-03 (commit `e94c38e`). `reasoner-worker.js`, the `PI_VOICE_OF_REASON_{MODEL,ENDPOINT,KEY_ENV}` overrides, and every z.ai code path are **gone** — do not go looking for them. `fff-subconscious-pi` still runs **`deepseek-v4-flash`** via its `config.json` `model` key, deliberately left alone: a fast retrieval role, and a config knob rather than a hardcode.
- `~/rig/extensions/voice-of-reason-pi/index.js` — upstream handles only the legacy **array** form of `event.systemPromptOptions.toolSnippets`. pi 0.75+ ships a `{name: snippet}` **map**, so upstream captures ZERO snippets on 0.79.10 and the tool briefing silently degrades. Patch coerces map → `name: snippet` strings.
- `~/rig/extensions/fff-subconscious-pi/` — three separate Windows breaks: `index.js` `startVenvBootstrap` used `spawn("sh")` + `python3` + `.venv/bin/python3` + `touch`; `observe.py` resolved the venv as `.venv/lib/python3.*/site-packages` (Windows is `.venv/Lib/site-packages`); `observe.py` imported `fcntl` at module scope. Patched with a `cmd /c` bootstrap branch, a two-layout venv probe, and an `msvcrt.locking` shim. All platform-branched, Unix path untouched.
- `~/rig/extensions/fff-subconscious-pi/config.json` — `canon_roots` shipped pointing at erenwork's **Forto** ingest dirs (`~/dev2-ingest-shadow/.../bundles-canonical`, `bundles-teamstalk`). Emptied. Do not restore.
- `~/rig/extensions/pi-memory/config.json` — repointed from erenwork's Mac path to `C:/Users/yepis/.claude/projects/C--Users-yepis/memory`, so pi reuses Claude Code's curated memory. pi-memory only ever writes `PI-MEMORY.md` and per-fact files, never `MEMORY.md`, so the two agents do not clobber each other.

## Build traps

- **`cortex-generic` does not run from a root build alone.** It proxies vendored sub-servers and dies on a missing `servers/github/dist/mcp/server.js`. `servers/github`, `servers/commands` and `servers/inspector` each need their own `npm ci && npm run build`. Its vendored `isession` sub-server always fails on Windows (non-fatal, cortex carries on).
- **`~/rig/forum/data` must be a nested second clone** of `esinecan/forum` — the MCP entry points at `forum/data/index.js`. A fresh clone has no `data/`. Node resolves deps up-tree from the outer `node_modules`, so only the outer repo needs `npm install`.
- `isession` is stdlib-only Python with **no `package.json`**. A vestigial 87-byte `package-lock.json` stub may appear in a clone and makes any "npm ci where a lockfile exists" rule hard-error; it is untracked dirt, delete it. Nothing to build, on any platform.

## Scheduled tasks — registered but DISABLED on purpose

Both exist and both are **disabled** as of 2026-07-28: a periodically-firing task flashes a console window, which the user did not want. Do not re-enable without being asked.

- **`isession-daemon`** — at logon, runs `~/rig/bin/isession-daemon.ps1` (local, deliberately not in the shared isession repo). Idempotent: no-ops if 8765 is already listening. Logs to `~/.pi/isession-daemon.log`.
- **`isession-wake`** — every 2 min, the repo's `bin/isession-wake.ps1` **with `-DryRun`**. Detects and logs only; drop `-DryRun` to let it fire pi. Drain semantics verified (reports a ready session once, then goes quiet), so live mode would not fire repeatedly. This is the task that was flashing windows.

**The daemon is now start-on-demand**: the `pi-collab` skill preflights port 8765 and runs the launcher itself. **Never stop the daemon or close a pi session on your own initiative** — the user keeps full-context pi collaborators alive far longer than looks necessary, and closing discards the accumulated context that is the whole point.

Gotcha when re-registering: `New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogOn` without `-User` means *any* user and fails Access Denied unelevated. Pass `-User "$env:USERDOMAIN\$env:USERNAME"`.

## pi's provider and skills

- pi runs **`zai` / `glm-5.3-flash`** (1M ctx, text+image). `zai-coding-cn` mirrors the same catalog through `open.bigmodel.cn` and now also serves glm-5.2/5.3 (it topped out at glm-5.1 until the 2026-08-16 catalog check); `zai` stays the default. Auth is the **`ZAI_API_KEY`** User env var; `auth.json` stays `{}` (pi only writes it via interactive `/login`, hand-authored shapes are rejected).
- **`models.json` no longer declares zai (2026-09-06).** pi 0.85.1 has zai built in with the same `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` baseUrl and the same `ZAI_API_KEY` resolution, and `models-store.json` already carries the whole glm-5.3 family, so the hand-written `zai` provider block was deleted as redundant. `models.json` now holds only `deepseek` (deepseek-chat / deepseek-reasoner, still absent from the store's v4-only catalog) and `openrouter` (stealth/ox-alpha). Backup: `models.json.bak-20260906-*`.
- **`--model glm-5.3-flash` alone is now ambiguous.** Four authenticated providers carry that id (`zai`, `zai-coding-cn`, `opencode`, `opencode-go`) and pi refuses rather than guessing. Pass `--provider zai`, or write `zai/glm-5.3-flash`. The default path is unaffected because `settings.json` names the provider.
- `--model X` alone re-resolves the provider (`glm-5.3` → `opencode-go`), so set provider+model together in `settings.json`.
- **OpenRouter / Ox Alpha, added 2026-08-25.** `stealth/ox-alpha` (1M ctx, 131k out, free while
  in stealth, reasoning mandatory) is declared in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` under the **built-in
  `openrouter` provider**, not a custom one. This is the load-bearing difference from dsh:
  **pi MERGES** custom models into a built-in provider (upsert by id, built-ins kept), where dsh's
  pi-ai adapter **REPLACES** the route's whole catalog with any `models` list. So on pi the entry
  is three lines and all 346 built-in openrouter models survive; verified by the absence of pi's
  `Model "X" not found ... Using custom model id` warning for `stealth/ox-alpha` and for a
  built-in id, and its presence for a bogus one. `baseUrl`/`api`/`apiKey` are all inherited and
  deliberately not restated, so `/login` auth applies. Backup: `models.json.bak-20260825-*`.
- **`pi update --models` will not find a stealth model.** It refreshed cleanly (touching
  `models-store.json`) but pulled no ox-alpha: OpenRouter's cloaked models are not in the
  generated catalogs, only in the live `/api/v1/models` response. Hand-declaration is the only route.
- **`/login openrouter` mints its own key** — "Sign in with OpenRouter" runs an OpenRouter PKCE
  flow (`openrouter.ai/auth`, present in the installed 0.84.2 build) and creates a user-controlled
  API key billed from OpenRouter credits, stored in `auth.json`. **No `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is needed
  anywhere**, which is why pi clears this where dsh cannot. On headless/SSH, paste the redirect URL
  into the prompt. Auth-file credentials beat env vars. Still do not hand-author `auth.json`.
- **`pi auth check` does not validate model ids** — a bogus model returns the same
  `credentials_not_configured` as a real one. It separates `provider_not_found` from
  `credentials_not_configured` and nothing finer; use a real `pi -p` run to test a model id.
- pi misreports its own identity ("I'm Claude"). Confirm routing with `pi --list-models`, never the model's answer.
- **pi and Claude Code read different skill dirs** (pi: `~/.pi/agent/skills/`, `<cwd>/.agents/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`; Claude Code: `~/.claude/skills/`), but they ARE bridged — see below.

## claude-skills-pi extension (built 2026-07-28)

`~/rig/extensions/claude-skills-pi`, in pi's `settings.json` packages. On `before_agent_start` it scans `~/.claude/skills`, parses frontmatter, and appends name + description + absolute path to pi's system prompt. Verified end to end: pi answered from the body of `housing-criteria` and cited it.

Why it works: **pi has no skill tool.** Skills arrive as one-line entries and the body is opened with the ordinary `read` tool — so a skill only needs *advertising*, not loading. Nothing is copied or symlinked. `config.json` `exclude` defaults to `pi-collab` (circular), `pi-dispatch`, `harness-guide` (Claude-specific, would mislead pi). Native skills are deduped.

pi's own `--skill <path>` flag and `"skills"` settings array are real (confirmed in source) but **were never observed working** on this box, even pointed at a single skill dir.

Two traps this cost:
- **CRLF frontmatter silently loses its last key** — the stray `\r` defeats `(.*)$` because JS `.` excludes `\r`. Normalize line endings before parsing. `notebooklm/SKILL.md` exposed it.
- **pi's self-reported skill list is confabulated.** A no-flag control run claimed `harness-guide`, which only exists in Claude's dir. Test with a canary fact from a skill *body*, never an enumeration.

## isession on Windows is mine

`isession/backends/windows.py` (ConPTY via ctypes, merged at `ceb73d2`) is erenhome's. Two traps worth remembering, both of which succeed at every win32 call and only fail under a supervisor — PORTING.md §10 now records them:

- **Std handles**: a child attaches to the pseudoconsole but its *stdio* is not bound to it. Without `STARTF_USESTDHANDLES`, `CreateProcessW` propagates the parent's handles, so a daemon with redirected stdio hands the child its pipes and all output bypasses the pty. `spawn()` blanks them across the call. **Testing from a terminal proves nothing** — the parent's handles are console handles there, so the bug hides.
- **Ctrl+C**: `GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent` cannot reach a ConPTY child (different console), and `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` *disables* Ctrl+C for the group it creates. Write `\x03` to the pty instead.

## Runtime traps (still true)

- pi accumulates orphan node/python children; it often prints its answer but does not exit, so `timeout` reports failure on a run that actually succeeded — **check stdout before believing the exit code**. Cleanup: `Get-Process node,python | Where-Object { $_.StartTime -lt (Get-Date).AddHours(-1) } | Stop-Process -Force`.
- Asking pi to enumerate every tool name stops completing within ~9 min once the fleet is 7 servers. Verify servers with `mcp({connect: "<name>"})` instead — far cheaper and it is how `forum`/`web-surfer` must be checked anyway, since they have no `directTools` and never appear by name.
- `--mcp-config <path>` REPLACES mcp.json wholesale, it does not merge.
